newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Thursdasy but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts said the market could begin to stabilise after having dropped sharply earlier in the week.

Analysts said the bourse, currently at 15,652.7 points, had tumbled after recent falls abroad and that though attention would be kept there, Polish shares might have reached a level where prices of some stocks had become attractive.

"I think prices have reached a corrected level in relation to the very high level that was," said Tomasz Berent of IB Austria Securities, referring to the bourse's three year February 18 high of 18,339.4 points.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 15,652.7 points and turnover rose 14.2 percent to 197.6 million zlotys ($64.4 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 38 to 33 with 22 stocks flat.
Analysts said there was a chance that if Friday's U.S. jobless data showed high employment and caused Dow falls due to expected interest rate rises, Warsaw stocks could fall more.
They said the market should find strong support at 15,300 should there be a lack of negative signals from abroad.
Analysts said it was difficult to predict Friday's price moves after Thursday's roughly balanced buying and selling after price-fixing and mixed continuous trade.
They said the main market's top gainer, industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim, rose 4.6 percent in heavy trade after Wednesday's plunge on news the firm had revised down 1996 net profits.
Analysts said the bourse's most heavily weighted stock should begin to stabilise with the overall market.
